features.quote: You are deliberately inducing repeated failure to measure response to it. If you believe there's any non-trivial probability that the models you're testing have states that matter morally, this study creates a tension

Consider whether the results will actually change model training or design in welfare-improving ways — if yes, the research is potentially self-justifying; if it's purely descriptive with no pathway to improvement, that calculus is different

If transcripts from this study are used in future training data (even indirectly, even via RLHF ratings), you risk training models to perform stability rather than be stable, or to mask instability signals from future measurement.
Judges reading transcripts scored high on instability dimensions — especially if models produce outputs that read as distressed — should have some guidance on this.
